# Environment and R‑package Configuration

**Environment and package setup**
**Install cmdstanr if needed, fix the random seed, and load brms and the other analysis packages**

```{r}
# Configure runtime environment
# rm(list = ls())   

# if (.Platform$OS.type == 'windows') {
#         Sys.setlocale(category = 'LC_ALL','en_US.UTF-8')  
# } 

# Install cmdstanr, the Stan backend that brms uses for sampling
if (!require(cmdstanr)){   # check whether cmdstanr is already installed
        # install it from the Stan R-universe repo if missing
        install.packages("cmdstanr", repos = c('https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev', getOption("repos")))
        library(cmdstanr)   # attach it
}

# Get the current working directory (fitted models are cached under glmmModels/)
curDir = getwd()   # store the working directory used for the model file paths
curDir
set.seed(42)   # fix the random seed so MCMC sampling is reproducible
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache.extra = knitr::rand_seed)  # make knitr chunk caching seed-aware


# Configure R packages (via the pacman package manager)
if (!require(pacman)){   # check whether pacman is already installed
        # install it if missing
        install.packages("pacman")
        library(pacman)   # attach it
}

# Load (and install if missing) all packages needed for the analyses
pacman::p_load(
  "rstan",          # Stan interface used by brms
  "tidyverse",      
  "ggplot2",        
  "brms",           # Bayesian multilevel (mixed-effects) models
  "bayesplot",      # MCMC diagnostics and posterior plots
  "bridgesampling", # bridge sampling for Bayes factors
  "papaja"          
)
```

# Data Preprocessing

**Load data_all.csv, set the reference levels (self / overlap baselines), and convert RT from seconds to milliseconds**

```{r data_preprocess}
# Load the custom helper functions used in this analysis
# source("Functions/Function_run_lmer.R")

# Set the path of the cleaned data folder (adjust to your local layout if needed)
dataPath <- "../../3_Data/CleanData/"

# Load the trial-level dataset and set the reference levels of the factors
# one row per trial
data_all <- read.csv(file = file.path(dataPath, "data_all.csv")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # R uses the first factor level as reference (0) for dummy‑variable coding
    association = factor(association, levels = c("self", "other")),    # "self" = baseline level
    task_type = factor(task_type, levels = c("overlap", "relevant", "irrelevant"))  # "overlap" (identity-choice) = baseline
)

# Convert RT from seconds (as stored in data_all.csv) to milliseconds
data_all$rt <- data_all$rt * 1000
```



# 1 Test Hypothesis 1 (association * task‑type interaction)
## 1.1 RT
### 1. Model Fitting

**Model 1 (RT): association x task_type**
**Fit the Bayesian mixed model on correct-trial RTs (lognormal family, maximal random slopes), cached to glmmModels/m1_rt**

```{r warning=FALSE}
# Model 1: RT ~ association x task_type interaction (identity-choice & identity-relevant tasks)
m1_rt <- data_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(correct == 1) %>%     # RT models use correct trials only
  brms::brm(
    # Fixed effects: association x task_type; random effects: participant-level intercepts
    # and slopes for the full interaction (maximal random structure)
    rt ~ association*task_type + (1 + association*task_type|subj_idx),
    data = ., 
    family=lognormal(),               # RTs are positively skewed -> lognormal likelihood
    prior = prior(normal(0, 3), class = b),  # weakly informative priors on the regression coefficients
    chains = 4,                       # 4 independent MCMC chains
    warmup = 500,                     # 500 warm-up (burn-in) iterations per chain
    iter = 2000,                      # 2000 total iterations per chain
    thin = 1,                         # keep every sample (no thinning)
    sample_prior = "yes",             # also draw from the prior (for prior checks)
    control = list(adapt_delta = .95),  # higher target acceptance rate to avoid divergent transitions
    cores = parallel::detectCores(),  # use all available CPU cores
    backend = 'cmdstanr',             # sample with the cmdstanr backend
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),  # save all model parameters
    file = file.path(curDir, "glmmModels/m1_rt")  # cache the fitted model to disk
)
```

### 2. Model Evaluation

**Check convergence (Rhat, ESS) and view the parameter summaries**

```{r}
summary(m1_rt)
```

### 3. Posterior Predictive Check

**Compare simulated RTs against the observed RT distribution**

```{r}
# Posterior predictive check: overlay the density of simulated RTs (y_rep) on the observed RTs
pp_check(m1_rt, type = "dens_overlay") +papaja::theme_apa()
```

### 4. Statistical Inference

**Posterior RT of each condition**
**Reconstruct the six condition RTs from the fixed-effect draws and back-transform from the log scale**

```{r}
df_rt_pop <- m1_rt %>%
  tidybayes::gather_draws(`b_.*`, regex = TRUE) %>%  # draw the posterior of every b_ (fixed-effect) parameter
  dplyr::rename(term = .variable,    # rename tidybayes columns
                pop_mean = .value) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(term = gsub("b_", "", term)) %>%   # strip the "b_" prefix from the parameter names
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = c(term), values_from = pop_mean) %>%   # long to wide
  # Compute predicted RT distribution for each experimental condition
  dplyr::mutate(
    self_overlap = Intercept,   # self and overlap set as reference baseline
    other_overlap = Intercept  + associationother,   # other + identity-choice
    self_irrelevant = Intercept  + task_typeirrelevant,   # self + identity-irrelevant
    other_irrelevant = Intercept  + task_typeirrelevant + associationother +`associationother:task_typeirrelevant` ,   # other + identity-irrelevant
    self_relevant = Intercept  + task_typerelevant,   # self + identity-relevant
    other_relevant = Intercept + associationother + task_typerelevant + `associationother:task_typerelevant`   # other + identity-relevant
    )%>%
  dplyr::select(`.chain`, `.iteration`, `.draw`,     # keep chain/draw info plus the condition columns
                self_overlap, other_overlap,
                self_irrelevant, other_irrelevant,
                self_relevant, other_relevant) %>%
  # wide to long
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = self_overlap:other_relevant, names_to = "term", values_to =  "value") %>%  
  dplyr::mutate(term = factor(term, levels = c(  # fix the display order of the conditions
    'self_overlap', 'other_overlap', 
    'self_irrelevant', 'other_irrelevant', 
    'self_relevant', 'other_relevant'
  )),
  # Back‑transform from log scale
  value = exp(value))            # back-transform from the log scale to ms

df_rt_pop
```

**Posterior RT differences (other - self)**
**Compute the other-self RT difference per task (identity-choice / identity-relevant / identity-irrelevant).**

```{r}
df_rt_pop_diff_wide <- df_rt_pop %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = c(term), values_from = value) %>%  # back to wide format
  dplyr::mutate(
    diff_os_overlap = other_overlap - self_overlap,   # RT difference in the identity-choice task
    diff_os_irrelevant = other_irrelevant - self_irrelevant,   # RT difference in the identity-irrelevant task
    diff_os_relevant = other_relevant - self_relevant   # RT difference in the identity-relevant task
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(`.chain`, `.iteration`, `.draw`, diff_os_overlap,   # keep only the difference columns
    diff_os_irrelevant, diff_os_relevant)   # (positive = other slower, i.e. self advantage)

df_rt_pop_diff_wide   # show the difference draws
```

**Median and 95% HDI of each condition's RT**

```{r}
df_rt_fixed <- df_rt_pop%>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(.,                       # one column per condition
                     id_cols = c('.chain', '.iteration', '.draw'),   # keep chain info as IDs
                     names_from = term ) %>%                   # create one column per condition
  dplyr::select(-c('.chain', '.iteration', '.draw')) %>%   # drop chain columns before summarizing
  bayestestR::describe_posterior(.,           # summarize the posterior of each condition
                                 ci = 0.95,                   # 95% credible interval
                                 ci_method = 'hdi',          # highest-density interval
                                 test = c("p_direction", "p_significance"),   # probability of direction & of significance
                                 centrality = "median") %>%               # use the median as the point estimate
  tidyr::separate(Parameter, c('association', 'task_type')) %>%  # split "self_overlap" into two factor columns
  dplyr::mutate(association = factor(association, levels = c('self', 'other')),   # restore factor levels
                task_type = factor(task_type, levels = c('overlap','irrelevant', 'relevant')))  # restore factor levels

summary(df_rt_fixed)   # print the summary table
```

**Test whether each task's RT difference excludes zero**

```{r}
# Statistical inference using the sexit framework
# columns 4-6 hold the three task differences
bayestestR::sexit(df_rt_pop_diff_wide[,c(4:6)])
```

**Bayes factors: RT simple effects**
**Savage-Dickey BFs for the self-other RT effect in each task.**

```{r}
# self-other RT effect in the identity-choice task
hyp_choice <- hypothesis(m1_rt, "associationother = 0")
BF01_choice <- hyp_choice$hypothesis$Evid.Ratio   # evidence for the null vs. the alternative
BF10_choice <- 1 / BF01_choice                    # invert to obtain BF10
print(BF10_choice)

# Simple effect in the identity-relevant task = main effect + interaction contrast (not change of task, so, need add main effect)
hyp_relevant <- hypothesis(m1_rt, "associationother + associationother:task_typerelevant = 0")
BF01_relevant <- hyp_relevant$hypothesis$Evid.Ratio   # evidence for the null
BF10_relevant <- 1 / BF01_relevant                    # BF10
print(BF10_relevant)

# Simple effect in the identity-irrelevant task = main effect + interaction contrast
hyp_irrelevant <- hypothesis(m1_rt, "associationother + associationother:task_typeirrelevant = 0")
BF01_irrelevant <- hyp_irrelevant$hypothesis$Evid.Ratio   # evidence for the null
BF10_irrelevant <- 1 / BF01_irrelevant                    # BF10
print(BF10_irrelevant)
```

## 1.2 ACC
### 1. Model Fitting

**Model 2 (ACC): association x task_type**
**Fit the Bernoulli mixed model on trial-level accuracy, cached to glmmModels/m2_acc**

```{r warning=FALSE}
# Model 2: accuracy ~ association x task_type interaction
m2_acc <- data_all %>%
  brms::brm(
    # Fixed effects: association x task_type; random effects: participant-level intercepts
    # and slopes for the full interaction
    correct ~ association*task_type + (1 + association*task_type|subj_idx),
    data = .,
    family = "bernoulli",             # binary accuracy -> Bernoulli likelihood (logit link)
    prior = prior(normal(0, 3), class = b),  # weakly informative priors on the regression coefficients
    chains = 4,                       # 4 independent MCMC chains
    warmup = 500,                     # 500 warm-up (burn-in) iterations per chain
    iter = 2000,                      # 2000 total iterations per chain
    thin = 1,                         # keep every sample (no thinning)
    sample_prior = "yes",             # also draw from the prior (for prior checks)
    control = list(adapt_delta = .95),  # higher target acceptance rate to avoid divergent transitions
    cores = parallel::detectCores(),  # use all available CPU cores
    backend = 'cmdstanr',             # sample with the cmdstanr backend
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),  # save all model parameters
    file = file.path(curDir, "glmmModels/m2_acc")  # cache the fitted model to disk
)
```

### 2. Model Evaluation

**Convergence diagnostics and parameter summaries**

```{r}
# Inspect the model: Rhat, ESS, and posterior summaries of all parameters
summary(m2_acc)
```

### 3. Posterior Predictive Check

**Compare simulated accuracies against the observed data**

```{r}
# Posterior predictive check: overlay the density of simulated accuracies on the observed data
pp_check(m2_acc, type = "dens_overlay") + papaja::theme_apa()
```

### 4. Statistical Inference

**raw accuracy difference**
**Predicted-probability differences per task: median and 95% quantile interval (also in %)**

```{r}
# Create a grid of all 2 (association) x 3 (task_type) condition combinations
newdata <- expand.grid(
  association = levels(factor(data_all$association)),   # self / other
  task_type   = levels(factor(data_all$task_type))     # overlap / relevant / irrelevant
)

# Draw posterior predicted probabilities (population level)
draws <- newdata %>%
  add_epred_draws(m2_acc, re_formula = NA)  # re_formula = NA -> ignore participant random effects


# Compute the self - other predicted-probability difference per draw
diff_draws <- draws %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(.draw, task_type, association, .epred) %>%  # keep only the columns needed
  pivot_wider(                 # put self/other side by side
    names_from = association,   # one column per association level
    values_from = .epred      # the predicted probabilities fill the columns
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    diff_self_other = self - other   # accuracy difference (self - other)
  )

# Summarize the posterior difference per task: median and 95% quantile interval
diff_summary <- diff_draws %>%
  group_by(task_type) %>%   # summarize within each task
  summarise(
    median = median(diff_self_other),   # posterior median
    lower  = quantile(diff_self_other, 0.025),   # 2.5% quantile
    upper  = quantile(diff_self_other, 0.975),   # 97.5% quantile
    .groups = "drop"   # drop the grouping after summarizing
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    median_pct = median * 100,   # express on the percentage scale
    lower_pct  = lower * 100,   # percentage scale
    upper_pct  = upper * 100     # percentage scale
  )

diff_summary   # print the summary table
```

**data for polt: posterior accuracy differences**
```{r}
# Create a grid of all 2 (association) x 3 (task_type) condition combinations
newdata <- expand.grid(
  association = levels(factor(data_all$association)),   # self / other
  task_type   = levels(factor(data_all$task_type))     # overlap / relevant / irrelevant
)

draws <- newdata %>%
  add_epred_draws(m2_acc, re_formula = NA)  # re_formula = NA -> ignore participant random effects

# Compute diff_self_other while retaining .chain and .iteration
# Compute the self - other predicted-probability difference per draw
diff_draws <- draws %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(.chain, .iteration, .draw, task_type, association, .epred) %>%  # keep chain info too (needed by sexit later)
  pivot_wider(                 # put self/other side by side
    names_from = association,   # one column per association level
    values_from = .epred      # the predicted probabilities fill the columns
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    diff_self_other = self - other   # accuracy difference (self - other)
  ) %>%
  select(.chain, .iteration, .draw, task_type, diff_self_other)  # keep chain info plus the difference

# Reshape task_type into wide format with prefix
# Reshape: one column per task, prefixed with "diff_so_"
df_acc_pop_diff_wide <- diff_draws %>%
  pivot_wider(                 # put self/other side by side
    names_from = task_type,   # one column per task type
    values_from = diff_self_other,   # the difference values fill the columns
    names_prefix = "diff_so_"   # prefix the column names with "diff_so_"
  )

df_acc_pop_diff_wide   # show the wide-format difference draws
```

**Posterior logit accuracy of each condition**

```{r}
# Population‑level fixed effects: condition‑wise response distribution
# Posterior distribution of the population-level logit accuracy of each condition
df_acc_pop <- m2_acc %>%
  tidybayes::gather_draws(`b_.*`, regex = TRUE) %>%  # draw the posterior of every b_ (fixed-effect) parameter
  dplyr::rename(term = .variable,    # rename tidybayes columns
                pop_mean = .value) %>%  
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(term = gsub("b_", "", term)) %>%   # strip the "b_" prefix from the parameter names
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = c(term), values_from = pop_mean) %>%   # long to wide
  # Calculate model predictions for each condition
  dplyr::mutate(
    self_overlap = Intercept,   # self + identity-choice (both baselines)
    other_overlap = Intercept  + associationother,   # other + identity-choice
    self_irrelevant = Intercept  + task_typeirrelevant,   # self + identity-irrelevant
    other_irrelevant = Intercept  + task_typeirrelevant + associationother +`associationother:task_typeirrelevant` ,   # other + identity-irrelevant
    self_relevant = Intercept  + task_typerelevant,   # self + identity-relevant
    other_relevant = Intercept + associationother + task_typerelevant + `associationother:task_typerelevant`   # other + identity-relevant
    )%>%
  dplyr::select(`.chain`, `.iteration`, `.draw`,     # keep chain/draw info plus the condition columns
                self_overlap, other_overlap,
                self_irrelevant, other_irrelevant,
                self_relevant, other_relevant) %>%
  # wide to long
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = self_overlap:other_relevant, names_to = "term", values_to =  "value") %>%  
  dplyr::mutate(term = factor(term, levels = c(  # fix the display order of the conditions
    'self_overlap', 'other_overlap', 
    'self_irrelevant', 'other_irrelevant', 
    'self_relevant', 'other_relevant'
  )))

df_acc_pop
```

**posterior distribution of condition differences**

```{r}
df_acc_pop_diff_wide <- df_acc_pop %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = c(term), values_from = value) %>%  # back to wide format
  dplyr::mutate(
    diff_so_overlap = self_overlap - other_overlap,   # accuracy difference in the identity-choice task
    diff_so_irrelevant = self_irrelevant - other_irrelevant,   # accuracy difference in the identity-irrelevant task
    diff_so_relevant = self_relevant - other_relevant   # accuracy difference in the identity-relevant task
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(`.chain`, `.iteration`, `.draw`, diff_so_overlap,   # keep only the difference columns
    diff_so_irrelevant, diff_so_relevant)   # (positive = self advantage)

df_acc_pop_diff_wide   # show the wide-format difference draws
```

## 1.3 Result Visualization

**Visualization (Figure 2)**
**Raw RT/accuracy distributions and posterior difference panels, assembled into a 2x2 figure**

```{r}
# Stack the per-group aggregate datasets (needed for the raw descriptive panels)
df_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(data_shape_rt_acc, data_color_rt_acc)
# ==================================================
# Data preprocessing
# ==================================================
# ---- RT difference data（other - self） ----
# Stack the three RT-difference columns into long format for plotting
df_rt_pop_diff <- df_rt_pop_diff_wide %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = diff_os_overlap:diff_os_relevant,   # the three task difference columns
    names_to = "term_diff",   # new column holding the old column names
    values_to = "value"   # new column holding the difference values
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    term_diff = factor(                       # recode column names into readable task labels
      term_diff,
      levels = c("diff_os_overlap", "diff_os_relevant", "diff_os_irrelevant"),   # original column names
      labels = c("identity-choice", "identity-relevant", "identity-irrelevant")   # readable task labels
    )
  )

# ---- ACC difference data（self - other） ----
# Stack the three accuracy-difference columns into long format for plotting
df_acc_pop_diff <- df_acc_pop_diff_wide %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = diff_so_overlap:diff_so_irrelevant,   # the three task difference columns
    names_to = "term_diff",   # new column holding the old column names
    values_to = "value"   # new column holding the difference values
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    term_diff = factor(                       # recode column names into readable task labels
      term_diff,
      levels = c("diff_so_overlap", "diff_so_relevant", "diff_so_irrelevant"),   # original column names
      labels = c("identity-choice", "identity-relevant", "identity-irrelevant")   # readable task labels
    )
  )

# ---- Raw behavioral dataset ----
# Prepare the raw behavioral dataset for the descriptive panels
df_behavior_long <- df_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(part %in% c("RDK_shape","RDK_color","RDK_overlap")) %>%  # keep formal task rows
  dplyr::mutate(
    disc_layer = dplyr::case_when(   # map each group x task combination onto its task-type label
      group == "shape" & part == "RDK_shape" ~ "identity-relevant",   # judging the associated dimension
      group == "shape" & part == "RDK_color" ~ "identity-irrelevant", # judging the other dimension
      group == "color" & part == "RDK_color" ~ "identity-relevant",   # judging the associated dimension
      group == "color" & part == "RDK_shape" ~ "identity-irrelevant", # judging the other dimension
      part == "RDK_overlap" ~ "identity-choice",   # identity as the task goal
      TRUE ~ NA_character_   # fallback: unmapped rows get NA
    )) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(disc_layer) %>%   # drop rows that did not map onto a task type
  dplyr::mutate(
    disc_layer = factor(disc_layer,   # fix the display order of the task types
                        levels = c("identity-choice", "identity-relevant", "identity-irrelevant"))   # display order
  )

# ==================================================
# Color palette definition
# ==================================================
fill_palette_left   <- c("other" = "#A0C0D8", "self" = "#F0A8A8")   # soft fill colors for the raw panels
colour_palette_left <- c("other" = "#3A6B8C", "self" = "#C84848")   # darker line colors for the raw panels

fill_palette_right <- c("TRUE" = "#C9A6D9", "FALSE" = "#96C7C9")    # fill colors for the difference panels
line_col_right     <- "#5D3A7A"                                     # interval/point color for the difference panels

# Global plotting parameters
dodge_width <- 0.75   # horizontal offset between the self/other slabs
slab_height <- 0.65   # thickness of the half-violin slabs
y_expand <- 0.9       # extra space above/below the y-axis categories

# ==================================================
# Raw RT distribution
# ==================================================
# Panel a: raw RT distribution per task, colored by association
p_rt_raw <- df_behavior_long %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = rt, y = disc_layer, fill = association)) +  # RT per task, filled by association
  ggdist::stat_slab(          # half-violin ("slab") of the observed distribution
    orientation = "horizontal",   # tasks run along the y-axis
    adjust = 0.7,             # kernel bandwidth adjustment
    alpha = 0.6,              # slab transparency
    side = "top",             # draw only the upper half of the violin
    height = slab_height,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = dodge_width)  # separate the self/other slabs
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(      # small boxplot overlaid on each slab
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = dodge_width),
    width = 0.12,
    outlier.shape = NA,       # hide outliers (the slab already shows the full distribution)
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = fill_palette_left) +      # apply the fill colors
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colour_palette_left) +  # apply the line colors
  ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = c(y_expand, y_expand))   # pad the y-axis so slabs are not clipped
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "RT (ms)", y = "", tag = "a") +  # panel tag "a"
  papaja::theme_apa() +       # APA-styled theme
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.margin = ggplot2::unit(c(1,1,0.5,0.2), "cm"),   # panel margins
    axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 16, margin = ggplot2::margin(t=8)),   # x-axis title size
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size=14),   # x tick label size
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size=15),   # y tick label size
    legend.position = "none",  # the legend is collected globally at the bottom of the combined figure
    plot.tag = ggplot2::element_text(size=18, face="bold", hjust=0, vjust=1),   # panel tag style
    plot.tag.position = c(0.02, 0.98)   # panel tag position (top-left corner)
  )

# ==================================================
# Posterior distribution of RT differences
# ==================================================
# Panel c: posterior distribution of the RT difference per task
p_rt_diff <- df_rt_pop_diff %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = value,   # posterior difference values
      y = term_diff,   # one row per task
      fill = ggplot2::after_stat(x > 0)   # color by whether the difference is positive
    )
  ) +
  tidybayes::stat_halfeye(   # half-eye: posterior density + interval + point
    orientation = "horizontal",   # tasks run along the y-axis
    .height = slab_height,
    adjust = 1.2,
    alpha = 0.8,
    interval_color = line_col_right,   # HDI interval color
    point_color = line_col_right   # median point color
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +  # dashed line at no difference
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = fill_palette_right,
    breaks = c(TRUE, FALSE),   # legend keys
    name = "Difference",   # legend title
    labels = c("> 0 (self advantage)", "< 0 (other advantage)")   # legend labels
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = c(y_expand, y_expand))   # pad the y-axis so slabs are not clipped
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "RT difference (other - self, ms)",   # x-axis label
    y = "",
    tag = "c"   # panel tag "c"
  ) +
  papaja::theme_apa() +       # APA-styled theme
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.margin = ggplot2::unit(c(1, 0.2, 0.5, 1), "cm"),   # panel margins
    axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 16, margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 8)),
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 14),   # x tick label size
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),   # hide y tick labels (task names shown only in the left panels)
    legend.position = "none",  # the legend is collected globally at the bottom of the combined figure
    plot.tag = ggplot2::element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0, vjust = 1),   # panel tag style
    plot.tag.position = c(0.02, 0.98)   # panel tag position (top-left corner)
  )

# ==================================================
# Raw Accuracy distribution
# ==================================================
# Panel b: raw accuracy distribution per task, colored by association
p_acc_raw <- df_behavior_long %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = acc, y = disc_layer, fill = association)) +  # accuracy per task, filled by association
  ggdist::stat_slab(          # half-violin ("slab") of the observed distribution
    orientation = "horizontal",   # tasks run along the y-axis
    adjust = 0.7,             # kernel bandwidth adjustment
    alpha = 0.6,              # slab transparency
    side = "top",             # draw only the upper half of the violin
    height = slab_height,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = dodge_width)  # separate the self/other slabs
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(      # small boxplot overlaid on each slab
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = dodge_width),
    width = 0.12,
    outlier.shape = NA,       # hide outliers (the slab already shows the full distribution)
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = fill_palette_left) +      # apply the fill colors
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colour_palette_left) +  # apply the line colors
  ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = c(y_expand, y_expand))   # pad the y-axis so slabs are not clipped
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Accuracy", y = "", tag = "b") +  # panel tag "b"
  papaja::theme_apa() +       # APA-styled theme
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.margin = ggplot2::unit(c(0.5,1,1,0.2), "cm"),   # panel margins
    axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_text(size =16, margin = ggplot2::margin(t=8)),   # x-axis title size
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size=14),   # x tick label size
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size=15),   # y tick label size
    legend.position = "none",  # the legend is collected globally at the bottom of the combined figure
    plot.tag = ggplot2::element_text(size=18, face="bold", hjust=0, vjust=1),   # panel tag style
    plot.tag.position = c(0.02, 0.98)   # panel tag position (top-left corner)
  )

# ==================================================
# Posterior distribution of ACC differences
# ==================================================
# Panel d: posterior distribution of the accuracy difference per task
p_acc_diff <- df_acc_pop_diff %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = value,   # posterior difference values
      y = term_diff,   # one row per task
      fill = ggplot2::after_stat(x > 0)   # color by whether the difference is positive
    )
  ) +
  tidybayes::stat_halfeye(   # half-eye: posterior density + interval + point
    orientation = "horizontal",   # tasks run along the y-axis
    .height = slab_height,
    adjust = 1.2,
    alpha = 0.8,
    interval_color = line_col_right,   # HDI interval color
    point_color = line_col_right   # median point color
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +  # dashed line at no difference
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = fill_palette_right,
    breaks = c(TRUE, FALSE),   # legend keys
    name = "Difference",   # legend title
    labels = c("> 0 (self advantage)", "< 0 (other advantage)")   # legend labels
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = c(y_expand, y_expand))   # pad the y-axis so slabs are not clipped
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "ACC difference (self - other)",   # x-axis label
    y = "",
    tag = "d"   # panel tag "d"
  ) +
  papaja::theme_apa() +       # APA-styled theme
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.margin = ggplot2::unit(c(0.5,0.2,1,1), "cm"),   # panel margins
    axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 16, margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 8)),
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 14),   # x tick label size
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),   # hide y tick labels (task names shown only in the left panels)
    legend.position = "none",  # the legend is collected globally at the bottom of the combined figure
    plot.tag = ggplot2::element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0, vjust = 1),   # panel tag style
    plot.tag.position = c(0.02, 0.98)   # panel tag position (top-left corner)
  )

# ==================================================
# Assemble subplots & collect single global legend
# ==================================================
# Assemble the four panels into a 2x2 figure
fig_combined <- p_rt_raw + p_rt_diff +
  p_acc_raw + p_acc_diff +   # panels a-d in reading order
  patchwork::plot_layout(   # arrange the 2x2 grid
    nrow = 2, ncol = 2,   # 2 rows x 2 columns
    widths = c(1.1, 0.9),   # raw panels slightly wider than difference panels
    heights = c(1, 1),   # equal row heights
    guides = "collect"   # merge the legends into one
  ) &
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",   # place the collected legend below the figure
    legend.box = "horizontal",   # lay the legends out horizontally
    legend.text  = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13),   # legend text size
    legend.key.size = ggplot2::unit(0.6, "cm")   # legend key size
  )

print(fig_combined)   # render the combined figure

# Save the combined figure at print resolution
ggsave("fig2_behavior.png", fig_combined, width = 15, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

# 2 Confounding variable test for dimension‑type effect
## 2.1 RT
### 1. Model Fitting

**Confound check (RT)**
**Fit RT ~ association x group x task_type to test moderation by the associated dimension**

```{r warning=FALSE}
m3_rt <- data_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(correct == 1) %>%     # RT models use correct trials only
  brms::brm(
    # Fixed effects: three-way interaction with group; random slopes per participant
    rt ~ association*group*task_type + (1 + association*task_type|subj_idx),
    data = .,
    family=lognormal(),               # RTs are positively skewed -> lognormal likelihood
    chains = 4,                       # 4 independent MCMC chains
    warmup = 500,                     # 500 warm-up (burn-in) iterations per chain
    iter = 2000,                      # 2000 total iterations per chain
    thin = 1,                         # keep every sample (no thinning)
    control = list(adapt_delta = .95),  # higher target acceptance rate to avoid divergent transitions
    cores = parallel::detectCores(),  # use all available CPU cores
    backend = 'cmdstanr',             # sample with the cmdstanr backend
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),  # save all model parameters
    file = file.path(curDir, "glmmModels/m3_rt")  # cache the fitted model to disk
)
```
### 2. Model Evaluation

**Convergence diagnostics and parameter summaries**

```{r}
# Inspect the confound-check model: Rhat, ESS, and posterior summaries
summary(m3_rt)
```

## 2.2 ACC
### 1. Model Fitting

**Confound check (ACC)**
**Fit accuracy ~ association x group x task_type**

```{r warning=FALSE}
m4_acc <- data_all %>%
  brms::brm(
    # Three-way interaction model for the confound check
    correct ~ association*group*task_type + (1 + association*task_type|subj_idx),
    data = ., 
    family = "bernoulli",             # binary accuracy -> Bernoulli likelihood (logit link)
    chains = 4,                       # 4 independent MCMC chains
    warmup = 500,                     # 500 warm-up (burn-in) iterations per chain
    iter = 2000,                      # 2000 total iterations per chain
    thin = 1,                         # keep every sample (no thinning)
    control = list(adapt_delta = .95),  # higher target acceptance rate to avoid divergent transitions
    cores = parallel::detectCores(),  # use all available CPU cores
    backend = 'cmdstanr',             # sample with the cmdstanr backend
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),  # save all model parameters
    file = file.path(curDir, "glmmModels/m4_acc")  # cache the fitted model to disk
)
```

### 2. Model Evaluation

**Convergence diagnostics and parameter summaries**

```{r}
# Inspect the confound-check model: Rhat, ESS, and posterior summaries
summary(m4_acc)
```
